Flavonols
Flavonols are arguably the most widespread of the ﬂavonoids because they are dispersed throughout the plant kingdom. The distri-
bution and structural variations of ﬂavonols are extensive and have been well documented. The most common ﬂavonols are quer-
cetin, kaempferol, myricetin, and isorhamnetin.
Flavones
Flavones have a close structural relationship to the ﬂavonols, but unlike ﬂavonols they are not widely distributed in plants. Their
only signiﬁcant dietary occurrences are in celery, parsley, and a few other herbs, and they predominantly occur as 7-O-glycosides
(e.g., luteolin and apigenin). In addition, polymethoxylated ﬂavones have been found in citrus fruits (e.g., nobiletin and
tangeretin).
